breath: Forecasting turns past observations into a best guess about the next period, and an error measure tells you how good that guess was.
startHere: This lecture is about guessing the next number in a series from the numbers before it, and checking how far off the guess was.
It matters because every later method in the course is compared with these simple forecasts.
Numbers recorded in order, one per period
A guess about a period that has not happened yet

sections.heading: Averaging the recent past
keyPoints: A moving average forecasts the next value as the mean of the last few values.
The window is how many values you average.
A short window follows changes fast; a long one hides noise.
blocks: A moving average forecasts the next value as the mean of the last few observations.
fromScratch: Say a kiosk sold 10, 12 and 14 coffees on the last three days. To guess tomorrow, add them and divide by three.

example.title: A 3-day moving average
example.result: The forecast for the next day is 23.

stuck.q: Which values go into the average?
stuck.a: Only the most recent ones, as many as the window says.

stuck.q: Why not average the whole series?
stuck.a: Old values may describe a situation that has changed.

blocks: The long-run direction of the series
A pattern with a fixed period

sections.heading: Measuring forecast error
blocks: MAE averages the absolute errors; MAPE expresses them as a percentage of the actual values.
